connections.why: Briefs must capture what real users actually need
User feedback drives each iteration of the design cycle
Final designs need clear visual communication to evaluate
Choosing wood vs metal depends on working properties needed
Polymer selection follows from strength, weight and finish
Each tool has specific safety considerations to learn
Different materials need different cutting and shaping tools
Both convert input motion into a different output motion
Programmable systems often drive mechanical outputs via motors
Structural choices depend on tensile and compressive strengths
Microbit/Arduino projects build on basic circuit understanding
Smart materials respond to inputs detected by sensors
Sketches develop into formal orthographic drawings or CAD models
CAD outputs are rendered and annotated for presentation
Textile choice depends on properties like absorbency and elasticity
Designing meals must respect dietary needs of the user
